previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___, a male with multiple myeloma on carfilzomib, chronic diastolic heart failure, type 2 diabetes, and autoimmune hemolytic anemia, was admitted for altered mental status and fever. He was found to have Listeria monocytogenes bacteremia and meningitis, confirmed by blood and CSF cultures. He was treated with ampicillin and gentamicin, with clinical improvement. MRI revealed a small acute infarct in the right precentral gyrus, but his mental status recovery suggested infection as the primary cause of AMS. He required transfusions for pancytopenia and had stable chronic kidney disease that improved during admission. His home medications were adjusted, including reduction in insulin and atenolol. He was discharged to a rehab facility to complete his antibiotic course and continue rehabilitation.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ with a past medical history notable for multiple myeloma s/p 
auto HSCT ___ w/ relapse in ___, currently on carfilzomib for  
___ years and recently started revlimid w/ admission for listeria 
meningitis here w/ fever, multifocal HCAP, course c/b ATN, rash, 
and delirium.

# Fever/HCAP: Presumed to be from Chest CT findings with 
consolidations. He had BAL done with unrevealing microbiology. 
He was followed by the infectious disease service, treated with 
vancomycin/cefepime/lefloxacin for broad coverage, and then 
narrowed to cefepime monotherapy for HCAP course. He completed 
his HCAP course during his hospitalization.  

# ___ on Chronic kidney disease: Creatinine 2.5 was above 
baseline 1.5, and plateaued and improving, with urine sediment 
suggestive of ATN, possibly from long exposure with gentamycin 
(renal toxicity also associated with carfilzomib and revlimid). 
There was not significant proteinuria to suggest manifestation 
of multiple myeloma. Renal ultrasound was within normal limits. 
Patient was transfused to have adequate intravascular volume, 
and intermittently diuresed given overall volume overload. 
Discharge creatinine was 1.6.

# Morbilliform Rash, likely drug rash, seen by dermatology. This 
was likely due to ampicillin, which he required for listeria 
coverage. Reassuringly, he was without mucosal erosions to 
suggest more severe reaction such as SJS/TEN, no suggestion of 
DRESS. Ampicillin was continued with rash symptomatically 
treated with topical sarna and triamcinolone. 

# History listeria sepsis/meningitis: continued ampicillin, last 
day: ___ (6 week course).

# Delirium: patient was found to have waxing/waning mental 
status during hospitalization. Workup consisted of MRI brain 
which was unrevealing for acute process. LP was performed and 
showed mildly elevated total protein (likely from prior 
meningitis) but gram stain negative and prelim culture without 
growth. Neurology was consulted and attributed symptoms to 
delirium, possibly due to cefepime. Cefepime dose was decreased 
and mental status improved. 

CHRONIC ISSUES:
# Right precentral gyrus CVA: continued ASA and statin

# Chronic diastolic heart failure EF 66%: patient received 
intermittent diuresis. His atenolol was discontinue and changed 
to carvedilol. Will need to address volume status at follow up 
appointments.  

# Pancytopenia: history of chronic AIHA and home 7.5 mg 
prednisone was continued 

# Multiple myeloma: S/p 28 cycles of carfilzomib with increasing 
 IgA paraproteinemia. He had received a single dose of revlimid  
as outpatient prior to admission. He was given IVIG during 
course.

# Type 2 diabetes: Insulin dependent. Per last ___ notes was  
on lantus 60 U qAM, glipizide XR 5 mg bid. Last A1c below goal  
at 5.6 in ___, so lantus was downtitrated on last admission 
to 40. During this admission patient had a few episodes of AM 
hypoglycemia and his lantus dose was adjusted. He was discharged 
on lantus 34U qHS. This dose should be uptitrated as tolerated 
to his home dose of 40U qHS while at rehab. 

#H/o atrial flutter s/p ablation: his home atenolol was 
discontinued due to renal failure. He was started on carvedilol 
which should be continued as an outpatient. 

TRANSITIONAL ISSUES:
======================
-Discharge creatinine: 1.6
-Discharge Antibiotics: ampicillin (last dose on ___
-Per neurology, set up as outpatient for Brain Fit Club
-CSF studies and BAL studies pending at the time of discharge 
-Patient had episodes of hypoglycemia while inpatient. Home 
lantus dose was decreased and adjusted while inpatient. 
Discharged on lantus 34U qHS. Would recommend increasing dose to 
40U qHS (home dose) prior to discharge if able to tolerate. Will 
need to restart home glipizide prior to discharge from rehab. 
-Discontinued atenolol and started carvedilol given renal 
function. 
-Will need to address volume status as an outpatient.

EXAMINATION:  CT CHEST W/O CONTRAST

INDICATION:  ___ year old man with hx of Myeloma. Recent listeria bacteremia,
meningitis. Vague cough. Recent chest xray with no consolidation now with temp
of 101.4. Please further evaluate.

administration of IV contrast.  Coronal and sagittal reformatted images were
also obtained.

FINDINGS: 

The thyroid gland is slightly heterogeneous and enlarged without focal
nodules.  There is no supraclavicular, axillary, mediastinal, or hilar
lymphadenopathy.  Atherosclerotic calcifications are seen at the aortic arch,
descending aorta, as well as the coronary artery extensively.  Calcifications
of the mitral annulus is also noted.  The right pulmonary artery is dilated
measuring up to 3.1 cm suggestive of underlying pulmonary arterial
hypertension.  The heart is mildly enlarged.  There is no pericardial
effusion.

The airways are patent to the subsegmental level.  Calcifications of the
tracheobronchial wall are stable.  There are consolidations at the right
middle lobe, right lower lobe, and to a much lesser extent left lower lobe
with air bronchograms compatible with pneumonia or aspiration.  There is a
small right and trace left pleural effusion.  No pneumothorax is seen.

The study is not designed for evaluation of subdiaphragmatic structures but
the limited included views of the upper abdomen demonstrates splenomegaly
measuring 16 cm, unchanged since the prior study.  2 mm left adrenal adenoma
is stable since ___.  Small renal cyst arising from the upper pole of the
right kidney is unchanged.

Multiple bony lucencies are noted in the sternum, thoracic spine as well as
the ribs compatible with known myeloproliferative disorder.  No acute
compression fracture is identified.  Incidental note is made of bilateral
gynecomastia.  A right chest Port-A-Cath terminates at the cavoatrial
junction.

IMPRESSION: 

1.  Multifocal consolidations in the right middle, lower, and to a much lesser
extent left lower lobe compatible with pneumonia.

2.  Extensive atherosclerosis.

3.  Dilated right pulmonary artery suggestive of underlying pulmonary arterial
hypertension.

4.  Bony lucencies and splenomegaly in keeping with history of
myeloproliferative disease.

EXAMINATION:  MR HEAD W/O CONTRAST T___ MR HEAD

INDICATION:  ___ male history multiple myeloma often with recent
posterior meningitis treated with 6 weeks of ampicillin and history of a right
precentral gyrus stroke currently being treated with HCAP, now experiencing
altered mental status and hallucinations.  Evaluate for stroke.

TECHNIQUE:  Sagittal T1 weighted imaging was performed. Axial imaging was
performed with gradient echo, FLAIR, diffusion, and T2 technique were then
obtained.

COMPARISON  ___ head MRI.

FINDINGS: 

There is significant motion artifact which degrades spatial resolution.

There is linear diffusion hyperintensity at the right medial precentral gyrus
(4 02:25) with questionable mild hypointensity on the ADC map.  On the B0
diffusion sequence there is T2 hyperintensity.  There is correlate FLAIR
hyperintensity without hemorrhage.  This is unchanged from examination of ___.

The remainder of the parenchymal signal is unremarkable.  There is unchanged
prominence of ventricles and cortical sulci consistent with a moderate degree
of volume loss.  The extra-axial spaces are unremarkable.  The vascular flow
voids are preserved.

The bilateral native lenses are absent, otherwise the orbits are unremarkable.
The calvarium and soft tissues are unremarkable.  There is a small mucous
retention cyst within the right maxillary sinus.  There is a right mastoid air
cell effusion which demonstrates intrinsic T1 hyperintensity (3:2; 5:8), which
is unchanged.

IMPRESSION:


1. Significant motion artifact which degrades spatial resolution.
2. Small linear diffusion hyperintensity at the medial right precentral gyrus
at the site of previously seen acute infarct from ___.  The degree of
diffusion hyperintensity and ADC mild hypointensity is greater than expected
for evolving infarct of this age, however there is hyperintensity on the B0
diffusion, therefore this reflects an evolving infarct with T2 shine through
or artifact rather than new acute infarct.  No evidence of hemorrhagic
conversion.  No evidence of acute infarct.
3. Unchanged right mastoid air cell effusion with intrinsic T1 hyperintensity,
likely due to chronic inspissated mucus.

EXAMINATION:  LUMBAR PUNCTURE (W/ FLUORO) N8 RF SPINE

INDICATION:  ___ male with history of multiple myeloma s/p auto HSCT
___ with relapse in ___, currently on Carfilzomib for ___ years and recently
started Revlimid admitted for listeria meningitis here with fever, multifocal
HCAP, and ___, now with altered mental status and hallucinations.  Lumbar
puncture requested for further assessment (in the past patient has required
multiple tries ___ bony malformations from MM).

TECHNIQUE:  After informed consent was obtained from the patient explaining 
the risks, benefits, and alternatives to the procedure, the patient was laid 
in prone position on the fluoroscopic table. A pre-procedure time-out was
performed confirming the patient's identity, relevant history, procedure to be
performed and labs.

Puncture was performed at L4-L5.

Approximately  5 cc of 1% lidocaine was administered for local anesthesia.
Under fluoroscopic guidance, a 18 gauge, 9 cm spinal needle was inserted into
the thecal sac. There was good return of clear CSF.  12 mls of CSF were
collected in 4 tubes and sent for requested analysis.

COMPARISON:  Lumbar spine MRI from ___.

FINDINGS: 

12 mls of CSF were collected in 4 tubes.

IMPRESSION:


1. Lumbar puncture at L4 5 without complication.
I, Dr. ___ supervised the trainee during the key components of
the above procedure and I reviewed and agree with the trainee's findings and
dictation.
